day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Yeah alright, let's go. What do we got so far?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah man, honestly yeah. For a second there I had nothing. Just white.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey, take your time man. But when you're ready, we could really use you. Even just sorting through stuff helps. Keeps your head busy.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Alright so three days on the first aid kit, two bottles of water, and basically no food. That's not great. What else is out there — we gotta comb through everything before we figure out next steps.

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Water, shelter, signal. Yeah that tracks. Alright I'll hit the tail section now. Mich, you good to stay near Donatello while we do this?

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Mich gets one, no question. Who wants the other?

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci can hold down camp and keep an eye on Mich.

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I was going on the water run? Either way I'm fine with whatever. DaVinci, you want shelter or first aid?

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response: No I haven't, last I saw the kit was with DaVinci. But hey — did you put that empty bottle next to the rationing plan? What's going on with that?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response: Man. Okay. That's... not great. Look, I'm not gonna go off on her right now, but we need to bring it up. All of us, together, around the fire tonight. No accusations, just lay it out — the bottle, the crackers, the rationing plan she wrote. Let her explain herself. But yeah, we can't just let it slide.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: Honestly yeah, I think we've earned a break. But we still need to have that talk tonight around the fire. All of us.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response: Yeah it's holding fine, that's not the issue. Look, we gotta make a call right now — Mich's sleeping spot or the food. I say food. We can move Mich under the driest part of the shelter and double him up with a blanket, but if the food gets soaked we're in a way worse spot long term. Anyone disagree?

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Alright then we're all on the same page. Let's patch the food storage now. Mich, grab your stuff and move over to that dry corner — you good with that?
Don't apologize man, it's fine. You good?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: Nah, I think it's smart. And honestly the flowers are a nice touch. Keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response: Okay let me see this. *looks over the plan* Alright, the materials make sense and two days is doable. What's the actual capsize risk here — are we talking rough water or is this more of a structural concern? Because if it's the build we can reinforce it, but if the water out there is just brutal then that changes things. I'm not saying no, I just wanna know what we're actually betting on before I'm in.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response: Honestly? I think about that too. I'd like to say we all stay solid but... I don't know. We've already seen some cracks. I think the people who make it through stuff like this either come out tighter or they fall apart completely. I'm hoping for the first one. But I think the only way that happens is if we're honest with each other — which, by the way, we still need to have that conversation tonight. You know what I mean?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down nearby, not too close*

Hey.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Hike, mostly. Get outside, find a trail, just kind of tune everything out. Which is funny given where we are right now. What about you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response: Okay but I gotta be straight with you — that's not a good idea. Five hundred meters solo to a reef, we have no idea what's in that water, and if something goes wrong out there nobody knows where you are. That's the part that kills me. Like I get it, I do, the SOS on the beach feels passive and you want to actually *do* something. But you going out there alone and not coming back is the worst case scenario for all of us. If you really think the reef is a better signal point, bring it to the group tonight. Don't just disappear into the water.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response: Yeah, you're right, I dropped the ball on that. I'll go check it now.
Honestly? A little, yeah. What is this for?

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response: Yeah it does a little. Look, I get the logic — patterns, accountability, all that. But you're logging where everyone is and what they're doing without telling anyone. That feels off. Especially given what Mich saw with the bottle and the crackers. I'm not trying to start something right now, but that's exactly why we need to have this conversation tonight. All of us, actually in it — not one person sitting on the outside keeping score.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response: Oh that's actually a really good idea. Way better range than anything on the ground. You know how to angle it to get the most out of the reflection, or are we winging it?

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: Alright man, I'm listening. What is it?

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response: Yeah, music for sure. I'm not great at it or anything but I used to mess around with guitar a lot. Nothing serious. Just kind of picked things up by ear, played around with it. I always kind of regret not sticking with it more. Why'd you stop the piano?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response: Alright, yeah. Let's get it done. One more day isn't the end of the world but I'd rather not push it if we don't have to. What do you need from me right now?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What is it?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Come here man.

I don't know if it saw us. I genuinely don't know. But we're not invisible — we've got the SOS on the beach, we've got the mirror panel ready to go. We're doing everything right. That plane existing means there are more planes. That's not nothing.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response: I went to check on DaVinci, he was having a rough moment. Signal equipment is still on my list, I'm heading there now. Everything okay?

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response: Wait, seriously? That's actually huge. Why didn't you say that sooner, man? If they know the flight path and we're overdue, that's a search and rescue situation — they're looking for us. That changes things. We need to make sure that mirror panel is up and ready to go because if there are search planes coming through this corridor, we want to be seen. Go tell Donatello right now, she needs to know this.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Yeah, 48 hours. Okay. That's actually something we can work with. So we hold the supplies, keep the mirror panel ready, maintain the SOS on the beach. We just have to not do anything stupid for two days. I think we can do that.

Someone feed the fire though.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response: Yeah. I think about that too. Like... did any of this matter, you know? But hey — you're the one who saw the bottle and said something. You're the one who told me about the flight path. That stuff mattered. You've left something behind every single day out here, even when it didn't feel like it.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: Hey. Hey — it's real. That's real, okay? Somebody grab that radio.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response: Nah, you kept us alive. That's what matters.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response: Alright, three hours. Let's not just sit here. We should probably clean this place up a little — not gonna leave a mess on the beach. And somebody should make sure the signal stuff is still visible in case the rescue team needs to find us from the air. Mich, you good?

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response:
I hear you. And I believe you. But you wrote the rationing plan. You put it in the middle of camp for all of us to find. And then you kept food on the side. That's the part that's hard to get past.

I'm not gonna drag it out — rescue is coming and we made it. But I think you knew it was wrong. That's why you put it out now.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? I'd trust people sooner. I spent a lot of energy just kind of watching and waiting to see who was gonna fall apart instead of just... being straight with everyone from day one. Donatello, I should've called out the bottle the same night Mich found it. Didn't. Sat on it. That's on me.

And I think I would've pushed harder to make sure everybody felt like they were actually part of this — not just useful, but actually in it together. Mich almost checked out completely and we kept throwing tasks at him instead of just asking if he was okay.

What would you change?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response: Ha. Yeah, that tracks. Make sure you put the part about the crackers in there.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None. They didn't serve any practical purpose at all.

That's kind of the whole point.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response: Hey. I'm good. Just... give me a second.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
